accepted: All five production avatars retain the v35 two-hand, five-digit articulation and now centre each visible-paddle middle-palm anchor on its existing solved grip point rather than placing the skeletal wrist pivot there.
Forearm and wrist targets are solved together from the reference hand-to-palm vector, avoiding a detached palm correction after the arm pose.
No-paddle rescue and swim states preserve their existing hand targets and relaxed digit articulation.
Matched and contact-side renderer evidence shows stable wrists, sleeves and digit chains with the shaft crossing the curled palm region more credibly than v35.
The UE 5.8 build, focused Python contracts and exact M5 production suite are green, including a 0.25 cm maximum palm-anchor error gate on every rendered production avatar.
rejected_or_open: The hand orientation still uses the shared reference wrist basis rather than a shaft-aligned per-action grip frame.
The coarse production hand mesh, generic curl profile and residual blade/shaft biomechanics remain visibly synthetic and prevent photoreal character approval.
The fingers do not yet use inverse kinematics, collision/contact constraints, grip sockets or motion-captured paddle strokes.
The broad seated posture, shoulder/elbow deformation and torso reaction remain procedural rather than trained synchronized rafting technique.
Raft, rock, broad water, foam/aerosol, shoreline, terrain, foliage and lighting remain below the requested photoreal bar.
No named guide or art reviewer has approved grip safety, hand placement, stroke biomechanics or capture, and neither frame is approved for release media.
renderer_iterations: v37 aligned palm-across anatomy to the shaft or T-grip with a 65-degree swing cap; it was rejected because foreground wrists produced a conspicuous twisted mitten silhouette.

v38 reduced the same assist to 28 degrees; it removed the worst twist but did not establish a clear two-view improvement over v36, so the orientation branch was fully removed and the exact v36 source hashes were restored.
